question: Which of the following is the best-known metabolic function of the lung

options.opd: Metabolism of basic drugs by cytochrome P–450 system

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Lung" -> "presence of ACE" -> "conversion of angiotensin-I to angiotensin-II" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Lung" -> "cytochrome P-450 system" -> "metabolism of basic drugs" -> "possible" -> 50%
analysis: The lung's most well-known metabolic function is the conversion of angiotensin-I to angiotensin-II. This is facilitated by the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), which is abundant in the pulmonary endothelium. While the lung also plays a role in the inactivation of serotonin and bradykinin, these functions are not as prominently recognized as the conversion of angiotensin-I to angiotensin-II. The metabolism of basic drugs by the cytochrome P-450 system is primarily associated with the liver, not the lung. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, the conversion of angiotensin-I to angiotensin-II is the most significant and well-known metabolic function of the lung.
